findings.where: Article specimen, from the photo caption to the subhead 'So, what are the key chapter topics?' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The subhead sits right under the photo caption, with almost no space between them, but well away from the paragraph it introduces. By proximity it reads as part of the photo-and-caption group instead of the start of a new section. The space above and below a subhead isn't kept to the rhythm the paragraphs use.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader skimming the article, who uses subheads to find sections and here sees a heading stuck to a caption. Also the founder: the brief asks the specimen to show that the rhythm holds when Angélique adds an image, a caption and a subhead, and this is exactly where it fails.

findings.where: Article specimen, the three-item list and the hairline rule under it (desktop and phone; worst on phone, where every item wraps)
findings.fault: The list's line spacing is much tighter than the body text's, and there's no gap between items. A wrapped line looks the same as the start of a new item, and 'Cycle.' runs straight into the rule and the related-lecture row below. The list is set on a different rhythm from the paragraphs around it, so the article's even rhythm breaks.
findings.who_objects: A reader going through Mark's list of chapter topics, who can't easily tell where one item ends and the next starts. Also the founder, since the brief makes the list part of the test of whether the type rhythm holds when Angélique adds content.

findings.where: First screen, the five outlined topic chips (PPP Law … Risk allocation) between the lead paragraph and the email action; on phone they wrap into three rows
findings.fault: The chips are white-outlined boxes, and the action under them is also a white box. By similarity they read as one set of buttons, so the one action stands out less. They also add a third band of detail between the message and the action on a screen meant to carry one message and one action. On phone, three rows of chips push the action further down.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from a development agency, whose eye goes to the row of pill buttons before the single 'write to me' action. Also the founder, who wants one message and one action and dislikes busyness (sheet §6).

findings.where: First screen, the large faint 'PPP' letters behind the heading, on top of the diagonal stripes on the field
findings.fault: The ghost letters fall behind the first three lines of the heading at a similar size, and their counters and stems cross the white letterforms. Together with the striped ground, that's two layers under the line that should stand clear. Figure and ground blur exactly where the page needs one large, clean serif line.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading Mark's line for the first time, who has to separate it from a second set of large letters behind it. Also the founder, who asks for one large line with scale contrast, not more elements, and who calls this kind of extra layer busy.

findings.where: Phone first screen: logo lockup, nav, full-width portrait, then the heading and the email action
findings.fault: On phone the portrait comes first at full width and fills most of the first screen, so the heading starts at its bottom edge. The email action sits about one and a half screens down, behind the lead paragraph and three rows of chips. The first view shows a face and a menu, but not his line and not the way to reach him.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone, who sees no message or contact without scrolling. Also the founder, whose brief asks for one message and one action on the first screen.

findings.where: Specimen parts below the fold on desktop: the Type pair row (the 'Gelasio' specimen beside 'Source Sans 3'), and the right-hand column below the Texture block and below the motion sketch
findings.fault: The two-column grid doesn't line up across the row. 'Source Sans 3' sits lower than the Gelasio specimen, and its note starts at a different height from the Gelasio note, so the two halves of the pair don't read as one row (continuity). Below Texture, and again below the motion notes, the right column leaves large empty gaps beside full left-hand content, so the specimen sheet looks lopsided.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the specimen parts as part of the tile. The type pair should read as two faces side by side, and the uneven columns make the sheet look unfinished.
